```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

spice reads SPICE3 netlists and runs SPICE3f5's device models and
analyses. In a few places its engine, Dune, does something else by
default than SPICE3 does — only where the result is measurably closer
to the converged answer at the same timestep. This vignette shows what
changes, and the one option that turns it all back.

```{r setup}
library(spice)
```

## The option

`compat` selects the profile of defaults: `"dune"` (the default) or
`"spice3"`. It can be given from R or on a `.options` card of the deck.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
spice_run(deck, options = list(compat = "spice3"))
```

Under `compat = "spice3"`:

* a transient integrates with the trapezoidal rule (Dune: TR-BDF2,
  which does not ring), and its step control uses SPICE's `trtol`
  allowance as is;
* a switch, or a `u()`/`sgn()` in a B source, flips at whatever
  timepoint first sees its control past the threshold (Dune: at the
  instant it crosses, located to `reltol` times the maximum step);
* LTRA lines interpolate quadratically, plant breakpoints by SPICE's
  rule and are not limited by their interpolation error.

Single options still win over the profile: `method = "trap"` under the
Dune profile integrates with the trapezoidal rule and keeps everything
else.

## A switch that is late

A relaxation oscillator: 10 V charges 100 nF through 10 kOhm, and a
switch across the capacitor closes at 7 V and opens again at 3 V. Its
period has a closed form.

<img src="figures/circuit-relaxation.svg" alt="Schematic of the relaxation oscillator: Vdd charges C1 through R1, and a switch across C1 is controlled by the voltage of C1 itself." />

```{r deck}
deck <- "relaxation oscillator
vdd 1 0 10
r1 1 2 10k
c1 2 0 100n ic=0
s1 2 0 2 0 sdis
.model sdis sw vt=5 vh=2 ron=100 roff=1e9
.tran 50u 20m uic
.end"

rp <- 1e4 * 100 / 1.01e4
vinf <- 10 * 100 / 1.01e4
exact <- 1e4 * 100e-9 * log(7 / 3) +
  rp * 100e-9 * log((7 - vinf) / (3 - vinf))
exact
```

The periods of a run are the spacings of the peaks of the capacitor
voltage:

```{r periods}
periods <- function(res) {
  v <- res |> spice_tidy("tran", "v(2)")
  i <- seq(2, nrow(v) - 1)
  peak <- i[v$value[i] >= v$value[i - 1] & v$value[i] > v$value[i + 1] &
    v$value[i] > 6]
  diff(v$scale[peak])
}

dune <- periods(spice_run(deck))
spice3 <- periods(spice_run(deck, options = list(compat = "spice3")))
```

With the flip located, every cycle is the same and matches the closed
form:

```{r dune}
range(dune / exact - 1)
```

On the 50 us grid of the deck the switch flips up to a step late, and
by a different amount every cycle:

```{r spice3}
range(spice3 / exact - 1)
```

## When to ask for SPICE3

* To reproduce a run of SPICE3 or ngspice, or to compare against one:
  `compat = "spice3"` is the profile Dune's own test suite uses
  against ngspice.
* When a deck was tuned around the trapezoidal rule's behaviour.

Otherwise the defaults are the better answer at the same cost: over
the engine's corpus of transient decks, the error at the deck's own
step is several times smaller for a few percent more timepoints.
